we introduce Grammar-Based Grounded Lexical Learning (G2LL), a lexicalist compositional approach toward learning grounded language from paired data, such as images and texts; we show that G2LL can learn to generalize from small amounts data to novel compositions in two different domains; we also present an algorithm that facilitates training in an exponentially-growing space of compositions; and we open-source our code and models to facilitate further research.
we propose a lexicalist approach towards learning a compositional meaning representation of language, and demonstrate that it generalizes well to novel compositions of language.

(1) we present a novel approach for learning a grounded lexicon from paired text and images; (2) we show that the lexicon is effective in learning compositional semantics and generalizes to novel compositions of known words; (3) we show that our approach is effective in learning visual reasoning skills and language-driven navigation skills.
